nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, Brzozowski's automaton of $M$ accepts exactly the language of $M$.
nodes.title: Brzozowski's automaton accepts the language of the original automaton

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the bijection from the states of Brzozowski's automaton of $M$ to the residual languages of the reachable states of $M$ that sends each state $p$ to the language accepted by $M$ from the state that $M$ reaches on $w$, where $w$ is a chosen word leading Brzozowski's automaton from its start state to $p$.
nodes.title: States of Brzozowski's automaton as residual languages

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states and words $w$ and $w'$, Brzozowski's automaton of $M$ reaches the same state on $w$ as on $w'$ if and only if $w$ and $w'$ are Nerode equivalent for the language of $M$, that is, have the same left quotient.
nodes.title: Brzozowski's automaton identifies exactly the Nerode equivalent words

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, every state of the intermediate Brzozowski automaton of $M$ (the subset construction of the reversal of $M$ restricted to its reachable subsets) is reached from its start state by some word.
nodes.title: Every state of the intermediate Brzozowski automaton is reachable

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the subset construction of the reversal of $M$, restricted to the subsets reachable from its start state.
nodes.title: The intermediate Brzozowski automaton

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the map that sends a state $p$ of Brzozowski's automaton of $M$ to the language accepted by $M$ from the state that $M$ reaches on $w$, where $w$ is a chosen word leading Brzozowski's automaton from its start state to $p$; this language is one of the residual languages of the reachable states of $M$.
nodes.title: Residual language of a state of Brzozowski's automaton

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the subsets of states of the intermediate Brzozowski automaton of $M$ that are reachable from the start state in the subset construction of its reversal.
nodes.title: States of Brzozowski's automaton

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, every state of Brzozowski's automaton of $M$ is reached from its start state by some word.
nodes.title: Every state of Brzozowski's automaton is reachable

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the subset construction of the reversal of the intermediate Brzozowski automaton of $M$, restricted to the subsets reachable from its start state. Equivalently: reverse, determinize by the subset construction and keep the reachable subsets, twice.
nodes.title: Brzozowski's automaton

nodes.summary: For a deterministic finite automaton $M$ over a finite alphabet with finite state set $Q$, the subsets of $Q$ reachable from the start state in the subset construction of the reversal of $M$.
nodes.title: States of the intermediate Brzozowski automaton

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, and let $L$ be its language. For a language $K$ and a word $w$, write $w^{-1}K = \{v \mid wv \in K\}$ for the left quotient of $K$ by $w$. Every state of Brzozowski's automaton of $M$ is reached by some word $w$; rename that state to $w^{-1}L$, which does not depend on the choice of $w$. The renamed automaton is exactly the minimized DFA of $M$: its…
nodes.title: Brzozowski's automaton is the minimal automaton

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finitely many states and $L$ its language, and write $w^R$ for the word $w$ read backwards. The determinized reversal of $M$ accepts exactly the reversed language $L^R = \{w \mid w^R \in L\}$.
nodes.title: The determinized reversal accepts the reversed language

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finitely many states in which every state is reached from the start state by some word, and let $L$ be its language. Write $u^R$ for the word $u$ read backwards, $L^R = \{u \mid u^R \in L\}$ for the reversed language, and $w^{-1}K = \{v \mid wv \in K\}$ for the left quotient of a language $K$ by a word $w$. Then two words $w$ and $w'$ lead the determinized reversal of $M$ from its start state…
nodes.title: Brzozowski's lemma

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finitely many states and $w$ a word. On input $w$, the determinized reversal of $M$ reaches the set of states $q$ of $M$ from which $M$, reading $w$ backwards starting at $q$, ends in an accepting state.
nodes.title: States reached in the determinized reversal

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with finitely many states, the determinized reversal of $M$ is the subset construction applied to the reversal of $M$: its states are the sets of states of $M$; reading a letter $a$ from a set $S$ leads to the set of states $q$ whose $a$-successor in $M$ lies in $S$; its start state is the set of accepting states of $M$; and it accepts exactly the sets that contain the start state of $M$.
nodes.title: Determinized reversal of a DFA

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
